clue.text: Display almost entirely red meat

indicators.note: almost entirely means the word red loses its final letter

parts.note: veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: A butcher's window shows off meat that is nearly all red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Display' looks like a noun but is the verb; 'almost entirely' drops the final letter of red.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to put it on display, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Take top off packing case for a price

indicators.note: taking the top off a word in a down clue removes its first letter

parts.note: a crate is a packing case

explanation.surface: Someone prises the lid off a crate and asks what it cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take top off' removes the C of CRATE; in a down clue the first letter is the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A rate is a charge or price asked, as in the going rate for a job.

clue.text: Here is some advert I got for dizziness

indicators.note: some of these words means only part of their letters are taken, running across them

explanation.surface: An advertiser admits the advert gave them a spinning head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to a run inside 'advert I got'; 'Here is' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a sensation of whirling giddiness, a direct synonym for dizziness.

clue.text: Tea set he repaired for one who loves beautiful things

indicators.note: repaired suggests the letters of the tea set are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A man mends a broken tea set, as only an art lover would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges the letters of TEA SET HE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is a person devoted to art and beauty.

clue.text: Encouraging one at the bookie's?

parts.note: one gives the article A
what goes on at a bookmaker's shop is betting

explanation.surface: Someone at the betting shop is egging on a fellow punter.
explanation.walkthrough: A BOOKIE'S (bookmaker's) is a British betting shop; aiding and abetting means encouraging wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Abetting means urging on or supporting someone, usually in wrongdoing, so it matches encouraging.

clue.text: Revive one big flirt after a collapse

indicators.note: a collapse knocks the words one big flirt down so that their letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A flirt brings themself back round after fainting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a collapse' rearranges all eleven letters of ONE BIG FLIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: To revive something is to restore it, an idiom equivalent to making it live again.

clue.text: Crowds turning up for play about love

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
about means one piece goes around another

parts.note: sport is play or fun
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Audiences arrive in numbers for a romantic drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside SPORT to make SPOORT; 'turning up' reads that upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops can mean groups or crowds of people moving together, a verb or noun sense of throngs.

clue.text: Be left in it, squeezing her

indicators.note: squeezing means the words in it press around another piece

parts.note: the two words taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck in a tight spot with a woman pressed in beside them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be left' reads as a direction or a remainder, but it means receive under a will; 'squeezing' splits 'in it' around the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to be left property in a will.

clue.text: Heavy part of uniform seen in famous film

parts.note: great can mean famous, as in the great and the good
a film is a thin coat or layer

explanation.surface: A soldier's heavy coat is spotted in a celebrated movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is not a movie here but a thin layer, COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A greatcoat is a heavy overcoat worn as military uniform.

clue.text: Care taken about hospital jab

indicators.note: taken about means one piece is placed around another

parts.note: to have in one's care is to have in trust

explanation.surface: Nursing care is provided around a hospital injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken about' wraps TRUST around H.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrust is a sudden poke or jab with a weapon or the fist.

clue.text: No child divides a pile in this game

indicators.note: divides means a piece splits another word by going into it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: No youngster splits a heap of something in this pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divides' splits the pile after its second letter; 'this game' is the definition, with 'in' and 'a' as links.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinochle is an American card game, so it is one example of a game.

clue.text: Quarrelling with inner self demands courage

parts.note: quarrelling is fighting
the spirit is a person's inner self or soul

explanation.surface: Arguing with your own conscience takes nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demands' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting spirit is an idiom for the willingness to keep going, that is bravery.

clue.text: Unconquerable in the party, Tim returns with gifts

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party

indicators.note: returns means the name Tim is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written
able means talented, endowed with gifts

explanation.surface: At a party, Tim comes back bringing presents and cannot be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses TIM to MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Indomitable means impossible to subdue, a synonym for unconquerable.

clue.text: Turning cross before turning cross at each house in turn

indicators.note: turning means the word for cross is written back to front

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix
to means before, as in ten to six

indicators.note: turning again reverses the second word for cross

parts.note: rood again, the cross in a church

explanation.surface: A grumpy person makes their rounds, getting crosser at every door.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Turning' and 'turning' reverse ROOD to DOOR; ROOD is an old word for a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: Door-to-door describes visiting every house along a street in sequence.

clue.text: Repudiation lies in PM's street

indicators.note: in places one piece within another word

parts.note: Downing Street is the home of the UK Prime Minister
lies in the sense of is located, giving is

explanation.surface: A rejection of untruths is coming from Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lies' is not falsehoods but 'is situated'. Downing Street is the home of the British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Disowning is a refusal to acknowledge or accept something, the act of repudiating it.

clue.text: Mr Preminger went this way and that

indicators.note: this way and that says the name reads the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A film director walks back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: Otto Preminger was an Austrian-American film director.
explanation.definitionFit: Preminger's first name, the director known for Anatomy of a Murder.

clue.text: See you charge correctly!

parts.note: a fare is a charge for travel
well means properly or correctly

explanation.surface: A bus conductor signs off after collecting the money properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See you' is the definition, a parting phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is a goodbye, and 'see you' is a casual parting greeting.

clue.text: This house is holding me back

indicators.note: back means the combined letters are read in reverse
holding means one word contains another

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A house is restraining me from leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts the second word inside the first, then 'back' turns the result round. A SEMI is a British semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is a semi-detached house, one sharing a wall with its neighbour.

clue.text: Artist's new composition of "Sea Mist"

indicators.note: a new composition rearranges the letters of Sea Mist

explanation.surface: A painter's latest work is a seascape called Sea Mist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new composition of' rearranges SEA MIST; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Mabel in a TV revival, blowing hot and cold

indicators.note: a revival reshapes and restages the letters of Mabel in a TV

explanation.surface: Mabel stars in a TV revival and can't make her mind up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revival' rearranges MABEL IN A TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambivalent means having mixed feelings, an idiom-match for alternately keen and cool.

clue.text: Sheathe pen, disoriented with love

indicators.note: disoriented means the letters lose their bearings and come out reordered

explanation.surface: A lovesick writer fumbles to cap their pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disoriented' rearranges PEN and LOVE together; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap up or enclose, which is what a sheath does.

clue.text: Detective shows tax men nothing in the kitty

indicators.note: in places a piece within another word

parts.note: a pot is the kitty in a card game
IR is the Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An investigator finds the taxman has left the card players' pool empty.
explanation.walkthrough: IR is the Inland Revenue, Britain's former tax office. Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's Belgian sleuth, an example of a detective.

clue.text: Freely, like only eleven footballers?

definitions.meaning: a side of exactly eleven players has no substitutes on the bench

explanation.walkthrough: Football reserves are substitutes; a team of eleven alone has none.
explanation.definitionFit: Without reserve is an idiom for frankly and unrestrainedly, and literally a squad with no substitutes.

clue.text: She carries an egg that touches the pavement

indicators.note: carries means one word holds another inside it

parts.note: taken as written
an egg is O-shaped, giving the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman walks down the street holding an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' puts O inside SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear soles are what meet the ground when walking, a cryptic description of footwear.

clue.text: Carve, since rib can be minced

indicators.note: minced means chopped up, so the letters of since rib are jumbled

explanation.surface: A butcher carves because the rib can be minced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be minced' rearranges SINCE RIB.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe is to cut letters into stone or metal, so it means carve.

clue.text: Constitution of ex-PM holding on to the pound

indicators.note: holding on to means one word grips another inside it

parts.note: Edward Heath was a UK Prime Minister in the 1970s
L is the abbreviation for the pound sterling

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister clings to sterling for the sake of the nation's health.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward HEATH was British Prime Minister 1970-74; L stands for pound (from Latin libra).
explanation.definitionFit: A person's constitution is their physical condition or wellbeing.

clue.text: Bigwigs are naive when taking hold of a cash machine

indicators.note: taking hold of means one word grips another inside it

parts.note: green means inexperienced or naive
an ATM is an automated teller machine

explanation.surface: Important people are innocents who grab the cash dispenser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is a link word; 'naive' is the colour word for inexperienced, not a description of the bigwigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Great men are the important figures, the bigwigs of their day.

clue.text: Go by disguised, please

indicators.note: disguised means the letters of please are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: Slip past in disguise, I beg you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' rearranges PLEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse when it passes or goes by.
